items.help: Node identity; defaults to the hostname.
Directory for state.db, querylog.db, local.db, lists and keys.
DNS listeners: address and protocols (udp, tcp).
DNS-over-TLS listeners (RFC 7858, ALPN dot): address and tls {certFile, keyFile}.
DNS-over-HTTPS listeners (RFC 8484, HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1): address, path (default /dns-query) and tls {certFile, keyFile}.
DNS-over-QUIC listeners (RFC 9250, udp, ALPN doq): address and tls {certFile, keyFile}.
DNS-over-HTTPS over HTTP/3 listeners (udp, ALPN h3): address, path (default /dns-query) and tls {certFile, keyFile}.
HTTP API and UI listener.
Unauthenticated health listener (/healthz/*).
Prometheus /metrics listener.
Exact peers (CIDRs, normally /32) allowed to send PROXYv2 headers; loopback only when dnsdist shares the network namespace.
File holding the PROXYv2 TLV 0xE0 secret shared with the dnsdist supervisor (at least 32 bytes, e.g. openssl rand -hex 32); required when proxyProtocolFrom names a non-loopback peer.
Node-to-node listener (list bodies by digest, /internal/status); always TLS.
File holding the internal bearer token; empty derives it from the encryption key (KUDURRU_ENCRYPTION_KEY) with HKDF.
Internal listener certificate (PEM); empty issues one from the CA derived from the encryption key.
Private key for listeners.internal.tls.certFile.
CA bundle (PEM) trusted when dialling other nodes; empty trusts the CA derived from the encryption key.
Name verified in peers' internal certificates; empty uses the derived certificates' fixed name. Set it to a SAN of tls.certFile.
SO_REUSEPORT sockets per udp and tcp DNS listener, each with its own read loop (Linux; one elsewhere); 0 means GOMAXPROCS, 1 a single socket.
Store driver: sqlite (state.db under node.dataDir) or kube (CRDs via the apiserver).
How long to wait for the apiserver watches to sync before serving from local.db.
Oldest local.db snapshot that may still answer primary zones; older snapshots answer SERVFAIL while forwarding continues.
Named upstream groups: servers, strategy (parallel_best, strict, random, rtt_weighted), timeout.
Plain resolvers used to resolve upstream hostnames (DoT/DoH).

Suffix to upstream group map for conditional forwarding (longest suffix wins); a key may list several suffixes in dnsmasq form, "[/corp.example/10.in-addr.arpa/]". Conditional answers are never cached.

EDNS Client Subnet on upstream queries: strip (never send one; privacy default), forward (pass the client's own option), add (forward the client's option, else derive one from a public client address).
Longest IPv4 source prefix sent upstream in ECS (0-32).
Longest IPv6 source prefix sent upstream in ECS (0-128).
Maximum number of cached responses (LRU beyond it); 0 disables the cache.
Lower clamp for positive answer TTLs.
Upper clamp for answer TTLs.
Upper clamp for NXDOMAIN/NODATA TTLs (RFC 2308 SOA minimum otherwise).
Hits within prefetch.window that make an entry hot enough to refresh before it expires; 0 disables prefetch.
Window over which prefetch hits are counted.
How long past expiry an answer may be served stale when every upstream fails (RFC 8767); 0 disables serve-stale.
TTL of stale answers (RFC 8767).
How long a query for an expired entry waits for the upstream refresh before the stale answer is sent (RFC 8767 client response timer).
Apply blocklists to recursive queries; false answers everything unfiltered (temporary disable is a runtime toggle, not this key).

Block response when neither the Policy (blockMode) nor the BlockList (response) sets one: zeroIP (0.0.0.0 / ::, other types NODATA), nxdomain, customIP (blocking.customIP), refused (discouraged: stub resolvers fail over).
TTL of block responses when the Policy sets no blockTTL; short so a one-click allow takes effect quickly.
Report ready and serve while referenced blocklists are not loaded yet (queries are filtered by the lists that are loaded).
IPv4 answer for blocked A queries when the response is customIP; empty answers NODATA.
IPv6 answer for blocked AAAA queries when the response is customIP; empty answers NODATA.
Collect the per-node query log (querylog.db, rollups and the stats API).
Built-in query-log sink: sqlite (querylog.db with rollups; required for the dashboard) or slog (one JSON log line per query, nothing stored).
Privacy applied once at ingest, irreversibly: full, anonymize_client, hide_domains, hide_domains_clients or nothing (per-minute totals only). The answer summary is stored only in full.
How anonymize_client hides clients: prefix (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) or pseudonym (HMAC with a random in-memory key rotated daily; stable for a day, not reversible).
How long per-query rows are kept (rollups: 35 d per minute, 400 d per hour, daily forever); 0 keeps rows until maxDBBytes is reached.
Upper bound for querylog.db; the oldest rows are deleted first when it is exceeded. 0 disables the cap.
Names never logged: exact names, *.suffix wildcards (the suffix and everything below it) or /regex/.
Clients never logged: IP addresses, CIDR prefixes or client names.
Do not log special-use names (localhost, .local, .home.arpa, private and link-local reverse zones).
Refresh interval of BlockLists that set no spec.refreshInterval (at least 1m); the leader fetches, replicas pull by digest.

Blocklist loading at start: fast (serve at once from the disk cache, load in the background), blocking (not ready until every list is loaded), failOnError (blocking, and exit when a list fails to load).
Blocklist body cache (sha256(url) files); empty means <node.dataDir>/lists.
Per-prefix QPM rate limiting of UDP queries at ingress; TCP, DoT, DoH, DoQ and DoH3 are never limited, nor loopback clients and the health name.
IPv4 prefix length to queries per minute per prefix (token bucket holding one minute's allowance); merged with the defaults key by key, 0 disables a level.
IPv6 prefix length to queries per minute per prefix; merged with the defaults key by key, 0 disables a level.
Percentage (0-100) of over-limit UDP queries answered with an empty TC=1 response so real clients retry over TCP; the rest are dropped.
Most prefixes tracked at once (LRU); an evicted prefix starts with a full bucket.
CIDRs or addresses never rate limited (loopback always is).
Inline CRD-shaped objects (zones, lists, groups, policies); file-managed as file:kudurru.yaml and re-applied on start.
Directory of *.yaml object files, file-managed as file:<dir>/<name> and re-applied on change; deleting a document deletes the object.

TSIG keys (RFC 8945) for zone transfers and NOTIFY: name (referenced by DNSZone spec.policy.transferTSIGKeyRefs), algorithm (hmac-sha256, hmac-sha512) and secretFile holding the base64 secret (tsig-keygen format).
Local IP address outbound NOTIFY messages are sent from; empty lets the kernel choose. Secondaries must list it as a primary.
Log level: debug, info, warn, error. Per-role overrides as info,dns=debug.
Log format: json or text.
